facts.subject: IPC
facts.description: IPC stands for Inter-Process Communication and provides mechanisms for processes to exchange data and coordinate.

facts.subject: IPC
facts.object: Mechanisms for data exchange and coordination
facts.description: The fundamental purpose of IPC mechanisms.

facts.subject: Signals
facts.description: Signals communicate using event notification.

facts.subject: Signals
facts.description: Signals are defined as providing one-way communication.

facts.subject: Signals
facts.description: Signals utilize only a signal number for data size.

facts.subject: Signals
facts.description: The state of Signals persists until they are delivered.

facts.subject: Pipe (anonymous)
facts.description: Anonymous pipes transfer data as a byte stream.

facts.subject: Pipe (anonymous)
facts.description: Pipe maintains unidirectional data flow.

facts.subject: Pipe (anonymous)
facts.description: The Pipe uses a buffered storage size of approximately 64KB.

facts.subject: Pipe (anonymous)
facts.description: The Pipe connection persists until both ends are closed.

facts.subject: FIFO (named pipe)
facts.description: FIFO (named pipe) also facilitates data exchange via a byte stream.

facts.subject: FIFO (named pipe)
facts.description: FIFO maintains unidirectional data flow.

facts.subject: FIFO (named pipe)
facts.description: The FIFO uses buffered storage.

facts.subject: FIFO (named pipe)
facts.description: The FIFO exists and is maintained while the underlying file exists.

facts.subject: Unix socket
facts.description: Unix sockets can handle communication in stream or datagram mode.

facts.subject: Unix socket
facts.description: Unix sockets allow for bidirectional communication.

facts.subject: Unix socket
facts.description: Unix sockets offer flexibility in data sizing.

facts.subject: Unix socket
facts.description: The Unix socket connection persists while the file descriptor is open.

facts.subject: POSIX shared memory
facts.description: POSIX shared memory allows processes to access raw memory.

facts.subject: POSIX shared memory
facts.description: It enables both ways of accessing and sharing memory.

facts.subject: POSIX shared memory
facts.description: Shared memory supports arbitrary data sizes.

facts.subject: POSIX shared memory
facts.description: Shared memory persists until the shm_unlink operation is called.

facts.subject: POSIX message queue
facts.description: POSIX message queue manages communication via typed messages.

facts.subject: POSIX message queue
facts.description: Message queues support bidirectional message flow.

facts.subject: POSIX message queue
facts.description: The maximum size of a single message is defined by max_msg_size.

facts.subject: POSIX message queue
facts.description: The message queue persists until the mq_unlink operation is called.

facts.subject: eventfd
facts.description: eventfd utilizes a combination of a counter and notification mechanism.

facts.subject: eventfd
facts.description: eventfd allows for two-way event signaling.

facts.subject: eventfd
facts.description: The eventfd mechanism is limited to an 8-byte counter.

facts.subject: eventfd
facts.description: The eventfd persists until all associated file descriptors are closed.

facts.subject: signalfd
facts.description: signalfd represents a signal as a file descriptor.
